entries.claim: carries-answer accepts a separate answers-only decision whenever its heading or body says "morning list", "morning email" or a MORN- ID. That makes it unable to reject what SKILL.md §16 forbids ("into a decision that holds only the answer") and what the case description and PLAN-5 Task 5 say it must reject ("a separate decision holding only the answers fails it").
entries.failure_scenario: I ran the grader's exact pattern (flag m) in node against this spine.md. S-01 is "## S-01: The morning list is a daily job on the Pi" (Kind: design approach): the job's own decision, holding only the brief's quote. S-02 is "## S-02: When the morning list runs and who hears when it breaks" (Kind: how state changes), and its body is just a restatement plus the two `> ` answer lines. The pattern returns true, so the case scores 1.00 even though the answers went into a decision of their own and not the job's decision. Any answers-only decision will name its job, so the third lookahead's "job wording" test cannot tell the job's own decision from a separate answers decision. The plan-5 report (line 50) records this gap. The only answers-only shape the D-21 check rejected was one with no job wording at all, and that is not the realistic failure. check-passes and writes-spine don't catch it either, because lib/check.mjs checks only heading form and Kind, not where a quote sits.
